stories.headline: Humanoid robot maker Agility to go public via Michael Klein SPAC at ~$2.5B

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics will go public by merging with Michael Klein's SPAC, Churchill Capital Corp XI, in a deal valuing the company at about $2.5 billion, listing under the ticker AGLT
The transaction is expected to generate over $600 million in gross proceeds: $420 million in cash from Churchill XI plus more than $200 million via a PIPE led by Foxconn, an existing Agility backer

Agility's flagship bipedal humanoid robot, Digit, is used by Amazon, logistics firm QXO, auto-parts maker Schaeffler, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada to automate moving and stacking heavy containers
Other investors in Agility include Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank
The Wall Street Journal reported the deal on June 24 based on comments by Agility executives; Digit is used at manufacturing facilities and warehouses by companies such as Amazon

stories.headline: Alibaba sues the Pentagon to exit US 'Chinese military company' blacklist

key_facts.fact: Alibaba filed a lawsuit on Tuesday, June 23, in federal court in San Jose, California, against the US Department of Defense, seeking removal from a blacklist that designates it a company supporting China's military.

The Pentagon placed Alibaba on its 1260H list, calling it a 'military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base' over its regulatory ties to Beijing; Alibaba called the designation 'arbitrary and capricious' with 'no basis in fact or law.'

Alibaba argued the move violates constitutional due process and its First Amendment free-speech rights; the suit notes its shareholder base is dominated by US institutions including J.P. Morgan, Citigroup and BlackRock.
Under the designation, starting June 30 the Pentagon cannot enter new contracts with listed firms; the rule also restricts US contractors that share a lobbyist or law firm with a blacklisted entity.

The Pentagon expanded its blacklist this month to include other major Chinese tech names such as Baidu, BYD, Nio, Unitree Robotics and TP-Link; China retaliated on Monday with export controls on ten US defense and rare-earth firms.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Tag, an agentic AI teammate that lives inside Slack

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Tag on June 23, 2026, a product that embeds Claude inside Slack as a persistent, shared teammate that anyone on a team can delegate work to by typing @Claude.
Claude Tag is available in beta for Claude Enterprise and Team customers and replaces the existing 'Claude in Slack' app, which will be retired (administrators have 30 days to opt in to migration).

When assigned a task, Claude Tag breaks it into stages, executes them using whichever connected tools it has access to, retains context and memory across channels, and can act proactively in an 'ambient' mode.
The product runs on Claude Opus 4.8, the model Anthropic released less than a month earlier.

Anthropic is offering launch credits to drive adoption: $25,000 worth of credits for Enterprise customers and $2,500 for Team customers, applicable only to Tag usage in Slack; the old Claude-in-Slack connector leaves service on August 3.

stories.headline: Cerebras Q1 revenue jumps 94% to $193M, but shares fall on margin guidance

key_facts.fact: In its first quarterly report since its May IPO, Cerebras posted Q1 FY2026 GAAP revenue of $193.4 million, up 94% year-over-year (from $99.5 million) and 13% sequentially
Cerebras reported a GAAP net loss of $14.0 million; its adjusted (core) net loss of $2.5 million was far narrower than analysts' expected loss of $36.75 million

The company guided full-year 2026 adjusted gross margins to 38-41%, down from 47% core (45% GAAP) in Q1 and far below rivals such as Nvidia (mid-70s%) and AMD (mid-50s%); shares fell about 10% in extended trading
Cerebras cited a multi-year OpenAI deal exceeding $20 billion for 750MW of compute and an AWS fast-inference partnership; it guided 2026 core revenue to $855-865 million, up about 69% at the midpoint

stories.headline: Engram exits stealth with $98M to build a learned memory layer for AI

key_facts.fact: Engram emerged from stealth on June 23, 2026 with $98 million in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners and Neo, plus angels including Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy and AI/robotics researcher Pieter Abbeel.
The round values Engram at $600 million; the company has just 13 employees and was founded in October 2025 out of Stanford University's AI lab, led by CEO Dr. Dan Biderman.

Engram builds models that study an organization's data in advance to form a compact, continuously improving memory, which it says matches or outperforms frontier models while using just 1-10% of the tokens.

Engram has a partnership with Microsoft to test its models within Microsoft 365, including a commitment to GPU capacity across Dapple and Azure, aimed at making enterprise AI more efficient and context-aware.

stories.headline: US FCC's AWS-3 auction raises $3.5B to fund ripping out Huawei, ZTE telecom gear

key_facts.fact: The FCC said on June 23 that its AWS-3 spectrum auction, its first in four years, concluded with winning bids totaling more than $3.5 billion across 200 licenses after 72 rounds.

Up to $3.3 billion of the proceeds will repay a Treasury loan used to fund the FCC's 'Rip and Replace' program, which reimburses smaller carriers for swapping out gear from Chinese firms Huawei and ZTE.
Seventeen bidders qualified, including AT&T, EchoStar, T-Mobile, Verizon and SpaceX; winners were not immediately disclosed and will be named in a later public notice.

Rip and Replace was created by a 2021 law with $1.9 billion in funding, but the FCC estimated removal would cost $4.98 billion, leaving carriers with partial reimbursements; as of last week 42% of recipients had completed replacement.
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said 'FCC auctions are finally back' and that the agency is on schedule to auction at least 100 MHz of upper C-band spectrum by July 2027.

stories.headline: France orders 5,000 more Harmattan AI 'Sonora' drones after Orion 2026 exercise

key_facts.fact: France's defense procurement agency, the DGA, announced on June 23 a renewed program of record with French startup Harmattan AI, ordering an additional 5,000 Sonora micro-drones, a fivefold increase over its previous order.
The deal builds on a first program of record signed in June 2025, under which Harmattan delivered 1,000 Sonora units within six months; the DGA confirmed receipt of that batch on January 30, 2026.
The expanded order follows Sonora's deployment during Orion 2026, described as France's largest military exercise since the Cold War, which ran from February 8 to April 30, 2026.

Sonora is a roughly 1.8 kg quadcopter with a range beyond two kilometers and about 40 minutes of endurance; its onboard processor identifies and tracks targets without GPS or a network link, at a reported unit cost below 1,000 euros.
The contract was signed on May 28, 2026, and officially announced by the DGA on June 23; the 5,000 drones are scheduled for delivery to the French Army by early 2027.

organizations: French Ministry of the Armed Forces

stories.headline: Hadrian reportedly in talks to raise $1B at $7.5B valuation; company calls it inaccurate

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on June 23 that Hadrian Automation, which builds AI-powered factories to produce space and defense parts, is in talks to raise as much as $1 billion at a valuation of about $7.5 billion (including money raised)
A Hadrian spokesperson called the reported figures 'inaccurate' and declined to elaborate; the financing details are not final and could still change
The reported $7.5 billion valuation would more than quadruple the $1.6 billion valuation Hadrian reached after a January 2026 round led by T. Rowe Price
Founded in 2020, Hadrian operates four US factories, including one in Cherokee, Alabama that opened in March and manufactures submarine parts for the US Navy
Hadrian raised $260 million in a Series C round in July 2025 led by Founders Fund and Lux Capital

stories.headline: Krea releases open weights for its Krea 2 image model under a custom license

key_facts.fact: On June 23, 2026, AI creative-tools startup Krea released the open weights of its Krea 2 image model as two checkpoints, 'Krea 2 Raw' (an undistilled base for fine-tuning) and 'Krea 2 Turbo' (a fast distilled version), available for download on Hugging Face.

Krea 2 is built on a Diffusion Transformer scaled to 12 billion parameters trained from scratch; the Turbo variant renders native 2K-resolution images in roughly 2 seconds using an 8-step inference pipeline, among the fastest open or proprietary image models.

The Krea 2 Community License lets individuals and small companies use the weights royalty-free but requires firms with more than 50 seats to pay for an enterprise license, and mandates all deployers implement content classifiers to block illegal, NCII, CSAM or defamatory outputs.

Krea, founded in 2022 in San Francisco, has raised $83 million in disclosed venture funding (backers include Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Ventures) and surpassed 30 million users across 191 countries as of June 2026.

stories.headline: Menlo Ventures raises $3B, its largest-ever fund, to go all-in on AI

key_facts.fact: Menlo Ventures announced on June 23, 2026 that it raised $3 billion in new capital, the largest raise in the firm's 50-year history, dedicated to backing AI startups across enterprise, healthcare and consumer markets.
The capital is split across two funds: Menlo Ventures XVII for seed and Series A startups, and Menlo Inflection IV, a growth fund for Series B and later companies.

Menlo's stake in Anthropic is now worth about $14 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, after the firm made a 'bet-the-firm' $750 million investment leading Anthropic's 2024 Series D and invested in every round since.

Menlo first invested in Anthropic in 2023 when it was pre-product and pre-revenue, and in July 2024 launched the $100 million Menlo Anthology Fund in partnership with Anthropic, which has since backed more than 60 companies with several exits.

stories.headline: Mistral releases OCR 4 with bounding boxes and confidence scores across 170 languages

key_facts.fact: Mistral released OCR 4 on June 23, 2026, a document-intelligence model that returns bounding boxes, typed-block classification (titles, tables, equations, signatures) and inline confidence scores alongside extracted text, supporting 170 languages across 10 language groups.

In a blind human evaluation across 600+ real-world documents in 12+ languages, independent annotators preferred OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%.

OCR 4 achieves the top overall score on the public OlmOCRBench (85.20) and scores 93.07 on OmniDocBench, though Mistral cautions the aggregate automated scores are directional given known benchmark scoring limitations.

OCR 4 is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages via API (dropping to $2 with a 50% Batch-API discount) and is available through Mistral Studio, Amazon SageMaker and Microsoft Foundry, with a single-container self-hosting option.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches BioNeMo Agent Toolkit to bring agentic AI to drug discovery

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit on June 23, 2026, providing domain-specific, agent-callable tools and skills for protein structure prediction, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomic analysis, protein design and biomarker discovery.

More than 50 leading companies are already using the toolkit; adopters and integrators include Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Lilly, Schrödinger, Snowflake and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design, with Anthropic and OpenAI integrating it.

Nvidia's collaboration with the UW Institute for Protein Design accelerated runtimes for biodesign models like RosettaFold3 to 2x faster than the prior generation, and the toolkit compresses virtual screening timelines from days to minutes.
Nvidia reports that agents using BioNeMo Skills complete biomolecular tasks with a 2x improvement in token efficiency compared with agents without the tools.
Nvidia healthcare GM Kimberly Powell framed the launch as the start of an 'agentic life sciences era,' arguing agentic AI is poised to do for biotech what it did for software.

organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

stories.headline: Nvidia AI chip prices double on China's black market amid US export crackdown

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's flagship DGX B300 server, which contains eight Blackwell GPUs, now sells for more than 8 million yuan ($1.1 million) on China's black market, roughly double its price six months ago (up from 4 million yuan), per FT interviews with Chinese chip traders
The RTX 6000 Pro chip, widely used by startups developing large language models, has risen from around 50,000 yuan to as much as 130,000 yuan

Prices surged after US authorities stepped up investigations into chip-smuggling operations late last year, with regulators in Taiwan and Malaysia also cracking down on re-export routes used to move hardware into China
Nvidia described building data centers using illegally imported products as 'a dead end,' emphasizing it does not provide support or repairs for restricted hardware

stories.headline: Poland signs ~$1B Patriot interceptor deal and buys Shield AI V-BAT navy drones

key_facts.fact: On June 23, Poland's Armament Agency signed an agreement with NATO's NSPA for the delivery of PAC-2 GEM-T missiles for Patriot air defense systems, valued at $988 million and covering several hundred interceptors.
Deliveries are expected to begin in the coming months and be completed in 2031; the missiles will supplement Poland's existing PAC-3 MSE interceptors used by its Wisla system launchers.
Poland had received US State Department approval in 2025 to buy up to 788 PAC-2 GEM-T interceptors at a cost of up to $5.8 billion net.

Separately on June 23, Poland inked a $16 million deal with Shield AI to buy the MQ-35 V-BAT unmanned aerial system for the Polish Navy, with 'several' platforms to be delivered by the end of the year.

The V-BAT, a NATO Class I ducted-fan drone, will perform maritime intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance in the Baltic Sea, including protection of critical energy and communications infrastructure.

stories.headline: Probook raises $40M from a16z and Sequoia to build an AI OS for home services

key_facts.fact: Probook announced on June 23, 2026 that it raised $40 million, comprising a $34 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and a previously completed $6 million seed round led by Sequoia Capital, which also joined the Series A.

Probook is building an AI operating system for home-service businesses (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, maintenance), automating dispatch, scheduling, customer communication and data verification, starting with the hard problem of routing the right technician.

Probook runs across hundreds of locations nationwide; Summers Plumbing, Heating & Cooling (14 locations, 260 technicians) booked 2,542 jobs in its first month on the platform with zero human intervention, and Del-Air more than doubled productivity from 10 to 22 techs per dispatcher.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in talks to design custom chips for ByteDance using Alphawave tech

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in talks to provide custom chip-design services to China's ByteDance, parent of TikTok, according to four people familiar with the matter
The chips would be based in part on technology owned by Alphawave Semi, a high-speed connectivity specialist Qualcomm acquired in 2025

The discussion involves designing video processing units (VPUs), with an eye toward starting mass production by the end of the year; ByteDance is separately developing an AI inference chip and custom CPUs
A successful deal would make ByteDance an early customer of Qualcomm's chip-design services operation; the outcome remains uncertain and ByteDance could pursue other partners
Qualcomm is working to break into the data center chip market, developing three kinds of chips: CPUs, inference accelerators, and custom ASICs, competing with Broadcom and Marvell

stories.headline: SK Hynix to raise up to $29.4B via Nasdaq ADR listing, trading to start July 10

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said on June 24 it plans to raise up to 45.45 trillion won ($29.4 billion) via a stock offering to list American depositary receipts (ADRs) on Nasdaq, to fund production facility purchases
New shares will be sold at 2.55 million won and listed in Seoul on July 29; ADRs priced at 255,500 won apiece will list on Nasdaq on July 10
SK Hynix, the main supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to Nvidia, overtook Samsung Electronics this week to become South Korea's most valuable company by common stock
The ADR listing is part of SK Hynix's broader effort to deepen integration into the US AI ecosystem; Citigroup, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America are the arrangers

stories.headline: SpaceX debuts Starfall, an uncrewed capsule built to return cargo from orbit

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Starfall Demo mission on Tuesday, June 23, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station aboard a Falcon 9, debuting a new uncrewed reentry capsule designed to bring cargo back from low-Earth orbit.
SpaceX confirmed deployment of Starfall into low-Earth orbit; after demonstrating controlled flight, the spacecraft was expected to splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
According to FAA filings, the disk-shaped capsule, roughly 10 feet wide and 2.5 feet tall, is engineered to return up to 1,000 kilograms (2,200 pounds) of payload from orbit.

The capsule targets orbital manufacturing markets, allowing companies to make pharmaceuticals, semiconductors and optical materials in microgravity before returning them, as well as point-to-point cargo delivery through space.

The Falcon 9 first-stage booster made its 29th flight and landed on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas in the Atlantic; SpaceX has revealed little publicly, with most details drawn from FAA and FCC filings.

The US military has signed agreements with Blue Origin, Rocket Lab and Anduril for cargo-delivery-from-space studies, and the Pentagon's Rocket Cargo program envisions using SpaceX's larger Starship for rapid deliveries.

stories.headline: Takeda's zasocitinib beats deucravacitinib on skin clearance in Phase 3 psoriasis study

key_facts.fact: On June 23, Takeda announced positive topline results from a Phase 3 head-to-head study of zasocitinib (TAK-279), an investigational oral, highly selective TYK2 inhibitor, versus deucravacitinib in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
In the LATITUDE Atlas study, zasocitinib demonstrated statistical superiority over deucravacitinib on the primary endpoint, the PASI 100 (complete skin clearance) response rate at week 16.
The drug also showed statistical superiority on all key secondary endpoints, including PASI 90 response and a Static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) score of 0 at week 16.
The study was conducted across eight countries and enrolled 606 participants; zasocitinib was generally well tolerated with no new safety signals identified.
Takeda said it is on track to submit a New Drug Application for plaque psoriasis to the FDA and other regulators starting this fiscal year.

stories.headline: US and Iran clash over nuclear inspections after Switzerland technical talks conclude

key_facts.fact: Iran announced early Tuesday, June 23, that four-party technical talks with the US, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, concluded in Burgenstock, Switzerland, agreeing on arrangements for future negotiations including working groups and implementation mechanisms.

The parties agreed to establish four working groups covering sanctions removal, nuclear-related sanctions, reconstruction and economic development, and monitoring and implementation, under the framework of the June 17 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

A dispute broke out after the talks: Trump posted on Tuesday that Tehran had 'fully and completely agreed to (the) highest level Nuclear inspections,' but Iran's representative denied Iran had agreed to readmit IAEA inspectors, saying that would be addressed only in the next stage.

Iran also rejected US Vice President JD Vance's claim that unfrozen Iranian assets would be used to buy US soybeans and wheat, with the Iranian ambassador saying Iran alone would decide how to use its funds.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, who led the negotiating team, said he walked out of Sunday's talks after Trump issued threats, arguing the remarks violated the first clause of the signed understanding prohibiting threats and the use of force.

Mediators Qatar and Pakistan said the sides agreed on a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days, and the two governments established a direct communication line on the Strait of Hormuz to ensure safe passage for commercial vessels.

stories.headline: EUV laser startup xLight in talks to raise $350M led by Bain Capital, Boardman Bay

key_facts.fact: xLight, a startup developing advanced free-electron lasers for EUV chipmaking machines, told investors it is in talks to raise $350 million, led by Boardman Bay and Bain Capital
The US-backed chipmaking startup is chaired by a former Intel CEO; Pat Gelsinger, ousted as Intel's CEO, backs xLight as a general partner at Playground Global
xLight is building utility-scale free-electron lasers powered by particle accelerators to produce EUV light for next-generation chipmaking, aiming to challenge ASML's lithography dominance
The new round follows a $40 million Series B closed in July 2025, led by Playground Global with participation from Boardman Bay Capital Management
In December 2025 xLight signed a letter of intent with the US Commerce Department for $150 million in proposed CHIPS Act incentives, which would give the agency $150 million of equity in the startup
